oot. I deleted `target/` and `calc` afterwards so no build outputs are submitted, so run `build.sh` before using it.

Speed on the four public workloads, against the LibreOffice baseline:

| Workload | Correct cells | Time | vs LibreOffice |
|---|---|---|---|
| aggregate (1,000 SUMIFS/COUNTIFS/AVERAGEIFS) | 1000/1000 | 0.10 s | about 54x faster |
| chain (60k formulas, 20k deep) | 60000/60000 | 0.05 s | about 2.7x faster |
| lookup (5,000 exact lookups) | 5000/5000 | 0.025 s | about 66x faster |
| mixed (10k formulas) | 10000/10000 | 0.03 s | about 15x faster |

The chain workload is the weakest. About 20 ms of its time is zip decompression, which I couldn't shrink further.

The behaviours I had to match to LibreOffice:
- Booleans act as numbers almost everywhere.
- Text converts to numbers in some contexts, and the "TRUE" string converts to 1.
- Numbers print to 15 significant digits.
- Sums use Kahan summation.
- Criteria in the *IF functions follow LibreOffice's rules.
- Approximate MATCH/VLOOKUP scan linearly.
- When several errors occur in one formula, the one LibreOffice reports is emulated.

Beyond the public set, I fuzzed random formulas and mutated public workbooks against LibreOffice. Plausible generator-style formulas agreed on all of 1,500+ cells in one batch. The deliberately nasty nested fuzz still had about 1% mismatches, mostly which error is reported when several occur at once.

A few cases still differ from LibreOffice. All of them showed up only in my own mutated data, not in the public examples:
- **Approximate lookups on unsorted columns:** MATCH or VLOOKUP with TRUE on a column that has outliers can return a different row.
- **Wildcards in approximate MATCH:** a wildcard key with match type 1 or -1 can return a different result.
- **AVERAGEIF on text:** AVERAGEIF over text cells occasionally disagrees.
- **Whole-column references:** references like `A:A` are not supported and return `#NAME?`.

`NOTES.md` has a short description of the approach.
